en_summary: @StockSavvyShay cites Mark Zuckerberg saying his AI agent took him from ordering Instacart twice a year to twice a week, about 50x more, simply by making shopping easier. He argues agent commerce could raise how often people buy, with $META owning both sides as personal agents talk to business agents, while $AMZN and $MELI benefit from more transactions on their platforms.
ko_summary: @StockSavvyShay는 마크 저커버그가 AI 에이전트 덕분에 쇼핑이 쉬워져 Instacart 주문이 1년에 두 번에서 주 두 번으로, 약 50배 늘었다고 말한 것을 인용합니다. 그는 에이전트 커머스가 구매 빈도 자체를 늘릴 수 있고, 개인 에이전트와 기업 에이전트가 직접 소통하면 $META가 양쪽을 모두 장악하며 $AMZN과 $MELI는 플랫폼 거래 증가로 수혜를 볼 것이라고 봅니다.
text:
Mark Zuckerberg says his AI agent took him from ordering Instacart “twice a year” to “twice a week” which is ~50x more often just by making shopping easier.

Thats what makes agent commerce so interesting because removing effort of buying things could dramatically increase how often people shop rather than just shifting existing purchases online.

And as personal agents start communicating directly with business agents, $META could own both sides of the interaction while $AMZN and $MELI benefit from more transactions flowing through their platforms.

text:
UBS sees 2027 as the inflection year for $CBRS with revenue growing ~4x to $3.3B before reaching ~$23B by 2030 with 46% operating margins.

The interesting part is Cerebras’s on chip memory advantage becomes way more valuable as AI agents make dozens of model calls per task with CS-5 targeting 10K tokens per second per user in 2027.

And with ~$25B in contracted backlog already equivalent to nearly half of projected revenue from 2027 through 2030, shares now trade below 20x 2028 earnings.

zh_summary: @munster_gene 表示，Muse、Grok Bot 和 Dot 這類個人化機器人黏著度極高，因此 AI 從補貼階段轉向付費階段應會很順利，就像搜尋一樣。他說這有助於解釋為何 $META 今天上漲 4%，而納斯達克下跌 2%，原因是其新的 Muse Wonder Bot 模型將收取每月 20 美元或 100 美元。
en_summary: @munster_gene says personalized bots like Muse, Grok Bot and Dot are so sticky that the shift from AI's subsidy phase to its paying phase should be smooth, much like Search. He says that helps explain why $META is up 4% today while the Nasdaq is down 2%, on its new Muse Wonder Bot model that will cost $20 or $100 a month.
ko_summary: @munster_gene는 Muse, Grok Bot, Dot 같은 개인화 봇은 한번 쓰면 끊기 어려워 AI가 보조금 단계에서 유료 단계로 넘어가는 과정이 검색처럼 순조로울 것이라고 말합니다. 그는 이것이 월 $20 또는 $100를 받을 새 Muse Wonder Bot 모델 덕분에 나스닥이 2% 하락한 날 $META가 4% 오른 이유를 설명해 준다고 봅니다.
text:

text:

And I think Bill Ackman has the better map of how this ends.

Burry's Oct 11 note is clear: he sold the common, bought junior preferred, and flagged a Treasury conversion of the senior preferred (SPS) into common — dilution of 90%+.

That risk is real on paper.
I just don't think it's the base case the Trump team is trying to deliver.

Here's why I side with Ackman:

1. The SPS has already been paid — economically.

Fannie and Freddie drew about $193B from Treasury after 2008.
They have since returned about $301B in dividends.

Ackman's point is simple: treat the senior preferred as repaid, don't invent a brand-new dilution event to wipe out private common holders.

2. Ackman's path preserves the common.

His three-step plan:
→ Treasury / FHFA amend the PSPA so the SPS is treated as satisfied
→ Treasury exercises its warrants for ~79.9% of the common
→ Relist on the NYSE while conservatorship continues

Government control stays.
Mortgage markets aren't disrupted.
Existing common isn't vaporized by a 90% conversion.

That is "walk before you run," not "convert and crush."

text:
$MU broke below $1,000 today after reports China’s CXMT plans to launch new server memory by year-end using a design that packs more memory into smaller chips despite U.S. equipment restrictions.

text:
Deutsche Bank upgraded $ASTS to Buy with a $93 price target calling Friday’s 10% selloff “misguided” as $SPCX moves closer to competing directly with mobile carriers.

What stands out is Deutsche values AST’s Ligado spectrum rights at ~$19B against a $23B enterprise value implying rest of the business is worth just ~$4B.

That leaves a ton of upside if AST secures up to $1B in Japan funding, expands its government business and benefits from carriers moving closer to AST as SpaceX becomes a direct competitor.

Last wk, S&P +1.2% & hit new ATH. 10/30yr ylds down 2-3bps despite WTI +1%. Impressive given semis -4% w/ $MU -4% despite solid earnings. Negatives were OAI actual ARR rev of $50B vs prior $70B belief & pulling of $NVDA backed Firmus neocloud IPO. USD +$0.23.

Breadth remained poor with just 35% of the S&P above its 50dma (though this was up from 25% at the end of the prior week.) The heavy weight Magnificent 7 did their part up 1.6% on average during the week. But their small cap brethren in the R2K declined 0.9%.

Different asset classes and different segments of the equity markets are sending mixed messages. 

On the positive side, the 10-year auction cleared at a lower 5.30% than the 5.32% it was trading at right before it closed. Dealers took only 2.5%. There was real demand at this rate which makes me more bullish on the sectors of the market that reached oversold levels earlier in October on the move higher in yields.

This brings me to bank earnings that start on Tuesday morning. The $KBWB (Bank ETF) is down 12.1% since its closing peak on August 14th. This is a very different message compared to the S&P up slightly (+0.3%) over that time. I am a big believer that credit is the lifeblood of the economy. Any further sell-off despite trading at oversold levels last week would not be a great sign.

China’s industrial profits rose +4.2% YoY in August, the weakest YoY growth since November 2025.

Pressure is particularly visible in consumer-facing industries, where profits are falling in autos, clothing, and furniture.

Domestic demand continues to weaken, with consumption growth slowing to near zero while manufacturers, property developers, and infrastructure builders are cutting spending.

For the first 8 months of 2026, industrial profits were still up +15.7% YoY, but the gains are becoming increasingly concentrated, with the electronics industry contributing ~66% of total growth.

At the same time, raw-material industries contributed +6.2 percentage points to the overall increase, supported by higher commodity prices.

Weak domestic demand is weighing on China’s economy.

FY2026 첫 11개월만의 적자가 1.97조 달러로 이 기간 역사상 세 번째로 큽니다. 경제가 강하고 실업률이 낮을 때 정부는 일반적으로 재정 적자를 낮게 유지하고 경제 약세 기간을 위해 대규모 재정 지원을 예약합니다. 이번에는 안정된 실업률에도 적자가 역사적 고수준입니다. 높은 정부 지출과 상승하는 이자 비용으로 경기 침체 없이도 적자가 예외적으로 큽니다. 대규모 적자는 미국 경제의 영구적 특징이 되었습니다. 개별 종목에 대한 언급이 없습니다.

The US deficit is surging despite low unemployment.

The cumulative US fiscal deficit since 2020 has surged to a massive $14.18 trillion.

Meanwhile, the 7-year average unemployment rate has fallen -0.4 percentage points, to 4.7% over the same period.

In the first 11 months of FY2026 alone, the US deficit totaled $1.97 trillion, the 3rd-largest for this period of the year in history.

When the economy is strong and unemployment is low, the government would typically keep fiscal deficits lower, reserving large-scale fiscal support for periods of economic weakness.

This time, however, the deficit is running at historically high levels despite stable unemployment.

This comes as elevated government spending and rising interest costs are keeping the deficit exceptionally large even without a recession.

Massive deficits have become a permanent feature of the US economy.

zh_summary: 關於「2009年和2020年的600-1000個基點赤字跳躍主要來自酌情刺激（ARRA，CARES）」。這在2001年衰退和1991年衰退中也是如此 - 赤字從峰到谷上升600個基點的GDP。而2009年和尤其2020年「酌情刺激」的原因是防止系統崩潰（和美債市場），因為他們需要把增長推回高於利率，否則面臨債務死亡螺旋，否則美債市場會崩潰。Druckenmiller在2021年CNBC上給了關於這個的採訪。沒有提及個股。
ko_summary: '2009년과 2020년의 600-1000bp 적자 점프는 대부분 재량 자극(ARRA, CARES)에서 왔다'에 대해. 이것은 2001년 경기 침체와 1991년 경기 침체에서도 사실이었으며 적자가 피크에서 트로프까지 GDP의 600bp 상승했습니다. 2009년과 특히 2020년 '재량 자극'의 이유는 시스템 붕괴(및 UST 시장)를 방지하기 위해서였습니다. 성장을 금리 이상으로 밀어 올려야 했기 때문이며 그렇지 않으면 부채 죽음 나선을 직면하거나 UST 시장이 붕괴했을 것입니다. Druckenmiller가 2021년 CNBC에서 이에 대한 인터뷰를 했습니다. 개별 종목에 대한 언급이 없습니다.
text:
RE: "The 600-1,000 bps deficit jumps in 2009 and 2020 came mostly from discretionary stimulus (ARRA, CARES)."

This was also true in the 2001 recession & the 1991 recession - deficit rose 600 bps of GDP, peak to trough.

And the reason for the "discretionary stimulus" in 2009 & esp. 2020 was to prevent systemic collapse of the system (& UST markets), because they needed to push growth back above rates or face a debt death spiral, or the UST market would have collapsed.  

Druckenmiller gave an interview about this on CNBC in 2021 👇

ko_summary: 저자는 인공지능 토큰 가격이 5월 이후 50% 넘게 떨어져 100만 토큰당 1달러 미만이 됐지만, 전반적인 가격 인하보다는 더 싼 모델로 사용이 이동한 영향이 크다고 했다. 오픈 모델이 상위 트래픽의 약 60%를 100만 토큰당 약 0.83달러에 차지하고, 유료 모델 평균은 6.03달러이며 $GOOGL, OpenAI, Anthropic이 고가 구간에서 경쟁한다고 했다. 평균 가격 하락이 $NVDA, $AVGO, $AMD의 컴퓨팅 수요 약화를 뜻하지는 않는다고 본다.
text:
AI token prices have fallen more than 50% since May to under $1 per million tokens but a lot of that reflects usage shifting toward cheaper models rather than broad price cuts.

Open models now account for ~60% of top model traffic at just $0.83 per million tokens while paid models average $6.03 as $GOOGL, OpenAI and Anthropic compete at the high end.

The AI economy is going to continue splitting between cheap intelligence driving massive usage and premium models retaining pricing power which is why falling average token costs don't necessarily mean weaker compute demand for $NVDA, $AVGO and $AMD.

zh_summary: 作者說 $OSS 是他「實體人工智能」組合裡最小的公司之一，而且一直在加倉。理由是該公司為無人機、軍用車輛與自主系統做加固型人工智能算力，傳統數據中心硬體無法上陣，一旦設計進軍事平台就不易替換。
ko_summary: 저자는 $OSS가 자신의 피지컬 AI 바스켓에서 가장 작은 회사 중 하나이며 계속 담고 있다고 했다. 드론, 군용 차량, 자율 시스템이 센서 데이터를 현장에서 처리할 때 필요한 러기드 컴퓨팅을 만들며, 일반 데이터센터 하드웨어가 들어가지 못하는 자리를 메운다고 한다. 군 플랫폼에 설계되면 교체가 어려워 매출이 붙을 수 있다고 본다.
text:
$OSS is one of the smallest companies in my 'Physical AI' basket and I’ve been adding because it builds rugged AI computing systems for defense platforms where traditional data center hardware cannot operate.

As drones, military vehicles and autonomous systems process more sensor data locally that's where OSS comes in by providing the high-performance compute needed for real time AI without relying on cloud.

What I also like is once OSS hardware gets designed into a military platform then replacing it becomes much harder creating a potentially sticky revenue opportunity as defense spending shifts toward autonomy across air, land and sea.

Shocking stat of the day:

$241 billion worth of French corporate bonds are now trading at lower yields than French government bonds.

This figure is up +1,621% from just $14 billion at the start of 2026.

This means ~38% of French high-grade corporate debt is now trading at lower yields than government bonds of similar maturity.

The gap between corporate and government bond yields is widening as investor concerns about France's deteriorating fiscal situation weigh on government debt.

As a result, internationally exposed companies such as L'Oreal, $OR, and TotalEnergies, $TTE, are increasingly viewed as safer alternatives to French government debt, unlike French banks, which remain more exposed to sovereign risk.

This is in stark contrast to normal economic conditions, when government bonds are traditionally viewed as the safest part of the bond market.

France's corporate bond market is increasingly being treated a safer bet than its government bonds.

text:

- Capacity 
- Qualifications (especially for custom DFB lasers)
- Technological

1. For capacity, they're coming online with 100M+ CW DFB lasers Q4 2027 (global supply is roughly ~608M EML/CW lasers currently per Trendforce). 

Obviously by 2027 global capacity is going to grow a lot, with $AAOI, $AVGO (3x expansion), and others coming online.  

But if you extrapolate their 2:1 statement, that implies 300m lasers/year long term coming from their own supply + external foundries. 

This is incredibly valuable during a shortage that was quoted to be 3-5 years, and $LITE stating they already have demand visibility into 2031...

And when suppliers have started to qualify many more (eg. 5-7 vendors vs. 2-3 earlier) due to bottlenecks. 

I'm sure a lot of how they achieve that staggering amount is due to their manufacturing process/yields (which is a moat).

ko_summary: 저자는 $TSLA 강세론이 3년에서 5년 안에 모든 차량호출 서비스가 기사 운전과 자율주행을 함께 제공하고, 무감독 자율주행이 과거 자동차 혁신처럼 범용재가 된다는 점을 아직 모른다고 했다. FSD를 무시하는 것은 아니며, 테슬라가 광고와 실행으로 선발 우위를 확보하지 못하면 지난 5년 전기차처럼 중국과 다른 제조사에 사업을 뺏길 수 있다고 본다.
text: $TSLA bulls still don’t get that within 3-5 years, every ride hailing service will offer both chauffeured and self-driving options for all their products (Uber Black, Uber X, Uber XL). It’s not that I don’t value FSD, it’s just that unsupervised autonomy will become a commodity just as every other innovation in the history of the automotive industry has become commoditized (and I don’t buy that this time will be different). Species and companies get wiped out by technological change all the time, crypto is no different.

While I agree that, at the macro level, if Bitcoin is susceptible then so is conventional banking, at the micro-level it's totally different.

If my bank gets hacked by AI, I will be reimbursed.

If my wallet gets hacked by AI, I have just lost all the money I had on it.

Traditional banking can iterate through problems like this much more easily than crypto can, so even if you are right that it will ultimately survive, have fun living through that.

.@DavidSacks on the time Peter Thiel saved PayPal:

“I really liked working with him. When he hired me, he basically told me, ‘I need people here who I can scream at.’”

“I think what he meant by that was, I need people who can scream at me too. People who will be honest, and you don't even have to worry about hurting people's feelings.”

“He's a great contrarian thinker. I think that was the unique thing he brought—he'd always come up with these strategic insights that everybody else had just kind of missed.”

“Right before the dot-com crash in early 2000, Peter was raising a financing round for us and we got something like $200M in commitments to invest at a $500 million pre-money valuation. PayPal had no revenue, no profits, and not even really a business model.”

“This is the peak of the dot-com euphoria. Everyone in the company was saying, ‘That's too cheap, this is a bad deal, we can't do this.’”

“He's like, ‘Take it.’”

“We got the deal done the Friday before Black Monday. If we had waited just one more day—game over. There would not have been a PayPal.”

“He was the only one who really saw the bubble for what it was.”

“If it wasn't for his contrarian thinking, we would have been swept away with the rest of the bubble companies.”
